name: Firaun
tagline: He called himself the highest lord. He trusted his army and his rivers. The water took him.
description: Watch the fall of Pharaoh, scene by scene: the god-king of Egypt, the enslaved Children of Israil, Musa's gentle word, the magicians who believed, the plagues, the sea that parted and closed, a faith declared too late, and the body kept as a sign. Told through the Quran.
outro: Travel through the land, then see how was the end of the deniers.

lines: Egypt was the greatest kingdom on earth.
Its king gathered his people and made a claim no man can make.
He split his people into classes.
One of them, the Children of Israil, he crushed:
their newborn sons killed, their daughters spared.
He pointed to the Nile and its channels.
Remember these rivers, flowing beneath him.
Allah sent Musa and his brother Harun to him.
Even to this tyrant, the command was to speak gently.
He gathered his best magicians against Musa.
The staff swallowed their tricks.
And the magicians, his own men, fell down in prostration.
He swore to cut off their hands and feet and crucify them on palm trunks.
They answered him without fear.

items.text: You believed him before I gave you permission…
So decree whatever you are to decree…

lines: Then sign after sign fell on Egypt.
Each time he begged Musa to pray for relief.
Each time it lifted, he broke his word.
Musa led his people out by night.
At sunrise Pharaoh came after them with his army.
The sea ahead. The army behind.
His people said: we are caught.
Musa did not look at the sea or the army.
Strike the sea with your staff.
It split, and each side stood like a mountain.
They crossed on dry ground.
Pharaoh drove his army into the same path.
Then the water came back.
As the water closed over him, he said: I believe.
The answer came:
The man who called himself a god
was brought out of the sea as a body,
for everyone after him to see.
He boasted of rivers flowing beneath him.
In the end the water was above him.
What he trusted was what Allah used to end him.
